candidate.answerReason: The marked offsets make the intersection the rectangle's center. Each shaded piece has area 13/4, so their total area is 13/2, matching D.

methods.label: Use symmetry and split into triangles
methods.explanation:
The equal one-unit offsets at opposite corners suggest using a half-turn to locate the intersection.

[Figure 1](figures/2016_AMC_12A_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(A\) be the top-left corner and \(C\) the bottom-right corner. Let \(P,Q\) be the marked points on the top and left sides, respectively, one unit from \(A\). Let \(R,S\) be the marked points on the bottom and right sides, respectively, one unit from \(C\). Write \(O\) for the intersection of \(PR\) and \(QS\).

A half-turn about the rectangle's center sends \(P\) to \(R\) and \(Q\) to \(S\). Thus the center is the midpoint of both connecting segments, so it is \(O\). Consequently, \(O\) is \(4\) units from each vertical side and \(\frac52\) units from each horizontal side.

Drawing \(AO\) splits the upper-left shaded piece into two triangles with bases \(AP=AQ=1\). Their corresponding heights are \(\frac52\) and \(4\), so this piece has area
\[
\frac12\cdot1\cdot\frac52+\frac12\cdot1\cdot4=\frac{13}{4}.
\]
The half-turn also exchanges the two shaded pieces, so they have equal areas. Their total area is therefore
\[
2\cdot\frac{13}{4}=\frac{13}{2}=6\tfrac12,
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses elementary half-turn symmetry and the base-times-height formula for triangle area.

methods.label: Subtract the unshaded triangles
methods.explanation:
The unshaded area can be calculated by pairing triangle heights that add to a full side of the rectangle.

[Figure 1](figures/2016_AMC_12A_Q08_question_fig1.svg)

Let \(O\) be the intersection of the two interior segments. Join \(O\) to the top-right and bottom-left corners. These new segments divide the unshaded region into four triangles with disjoint interiors.

Let \(x\) and \(y\) be the perpendicular distances from \(O\) to the left and bottom sides, respectively. Its distances to the right and top sides are then \(8-x\) and \(5-y\).

Two of the unshaded triangles have horizontal bases of length \(7\). Their heights are \(y\) and \(5-y\), so their combined area is
\[
\frac72y+\frac72(5-y)=\frac{35}{2}.
\]
The other two have vertical bases of length \(4\), with heights \(x\) and \(8-x\). Their combined area is
\[
\frac42x+\frac42(8-x)=16.
\]
These four triangles fill the entire unshaded region. Subtracting their areas from the rectangle's area gives
\[
8\cdot5-\frac{35}{2}-16
=\frac{13}{2}=6\tfrac12.
\]
Thus the answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
methods.levelReason: Only rectangle area, triangle area, and addition of complementary perpendicular distances are needed.
